#2201. Tottenham Hotspur vs. Ipswich Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 15:09, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 18:05

Separated by three places in the Premier League table, 12th-placed Tottenham Hotspur welcome Ipswich Town to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday seeking a return to winning ways on matchday 11.

Leeds United halted Spurs' three-match league winning streak before the hiatus, and the capital club now aim to begin a seemingly favourable run of fixtures with a positive result against the Tractor Boys.

Roberto De Zerbi could have been forgiven for entering the international break disappointed after Leeds ended his side's three-match winning run at the start of the month.

Spurs scored seven goals and conceded just once across victories of 3-1, 2-0 and 2-0 over Coventry City, Chelsea and Crystal Palace to close out October, following a creditable 1-1 draw with 10 men at Manchester United.

Returning to home comforts in the capital presents an ideal opportunity for the Lilywhites to regain winning momentum as they pursue a third consecutive triumph in front of their supporters after victories over Coventry and Palace.

The upcoming schedule will quietly please De Zerbi, whose team face Ipswich, Sunderland, Fulham and Hull across their next five matches, offering encouragement ahead of those encounters with bottom-eight clubs.

Having already collected eight points from a possible 12 against the other four sides in the bottom eight, Spurs, currently four points behind fifth-placed Chelsea, will target another victory that could lift them into the division's top half.

Overcoming Ipswich will be far from straightforward for the North Londoners, despite the Tractor Boys winning only one of their last six Premier League matches and losing three.

The defeats suffered by Gary O'Neil's men against Everton, Manchester City and Bournemouth have all been narrow, underlining their battling qualities.

With their other two matches outside a 2-1 home victory over Fulham producing draws against Nottingham Forest (1-1) and Hull City (2-2), the travelling supporters will hope for another competitive showing from the promoted side.

That ambition is tempered by Ipswich collecting just four points from a possible 15 away from home this season, although O'Neil's men have recovered from a 5-2 gameweek two thrashing at Manchester United to beat Palace 3-2 and draw 2-2 at Hull, either side of defeats of 1-0 at Everton and 3-2 at Man City.

Although they have conceded at least twice in four of their five away matches since returning to the big time, the travelling supporters will back their side to secure a positive result if they deliver another spirited performance outside Portman Road.

Spurs have several injury doubts ahead of this weekend's match, with Mykhaylo Mudryk (ankle), Martin Dubravka (knee), Savio (muscle), Mathys Tel (ankle), Lucas Bergvall (knee), James Maddison and Tosin Adarabioyo (calf) facing assessments, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert remain sidelined with knee problems.

Mohammed Kudus has yet to score a league goal this season, but the playmaker's three assists and ability to threaten from unlikely positions make him a potential match-winner for the home side.

No Spurs player has scored more league goals than Jan Paul van Hecke, a notable statistic for the two-goal centre-back ahead of Saturday's encounter with the Tractor Boys.

O'Neil's side, meanwhile, have five players with two goals apiece: Emersonn, Jack Clarke, Julio Enciso, Leif Davis and Zian Flemming.

While Flemming has yet to start for the visitors, with Emersonn generally preferred at centre-forward, the former Burnley man's two away goals make him a potential game-changer off the bench in North London.

Unlike Spurs, who have several injury doubts, the visitors are believed to have a healthy squad for their gameweek-11 trip to the capital.

Tottenham Hotspur possible starting lineup:

Kinsky; Porro, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Tonali, Fernandes; Kudus, Gray, Marmoush; Solanke

Walton; Greaves, O'Shea, Diop; Ouattara, Lukic, Palacios, Davis; Maeda, Enciso; Emersonn

Ipswich have scored four goals across their last two away matches, offering encouragement that their varied attacking threats can trouble a Tottenham side carrying several fitness concerns.

Nevertheless, the visitors' inability to keep opponents quiet on their travels should provide enough opportunities for Spurs to secure another home success.

#2198. Kilmarnock vs Aberdeen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 19 Nov 2026 15:30, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:33

Kilmarnock and Aberdeen face off in an early relegation six-pointer in the Scottish Premiership on Saturday at BBSP Stadium Rugby Park.

Killie are rock bottom in the Scottish Premiership table with nine points from 13 matches, while Aberdeen are just two points and one place above them.

Kilmarnock have shown glimpses of a promising side under Neil McCann, but their reckless defending is proving to be a major stumbling block.

They have managed just two wins in 13 league matches, losing eight of those encounters, and are enduring a particularly difficult spell, having suffered three defeats in their last four outings.

Killie have scored 13 goals this season, showing that they possess the attacking threat to trouble opponents, but their defensive frailties are turning into a recurring nightmare.

McCann's side have conceded 29 goals so far, more than any other team in the division, and unless they address that problem, climbing the table will become an increasingly difficult task.

The East Ayrshire club have won just once in their last seven matches, while their home form has been particularly poor, with only five points collected from six games and 15 goals conceded.

Earlier this week, Aberdeen appointed Mario Frick as their new head coach following the dismissal of Stephen Robinson.

There is an acute sense of instability at the club, with the former Liechtenstein striker becoming their fourth manager in 2026, following Robinson, Peter Leven and Jimmy Thelin.

Frick guided Vaduz to promotion in 2020 before helping Luzern avoid relegation in 2021, and he will need to work similar magic at Aberdeen as the club look to navigate their current crisis.

The Dons have lost four consecutive matches across all competitions and managed just one victory in their last six Scottish Premiership outings.

Aberdeen have collected only four points on the road this season, but they have lost just once to Kilmarnock in their last six meetings across all competitions.

McCann does not have any major injury concerns, with goalkeeper Maksymilian Stryjek his only absentee.

The 30-year-old is currently sidelined with a knee injury but is expected to return by the start of next month.

It will take time for Frick to get a better understanding of his squad, but his immediate priority will be to motivate the players and prevent another defeat in this crucial encounter.

The Dons, meanwhile, are without Lewis Mayo (foot), Chris Cadden (hamstring), Kristers Towers (knee), Emmanuel Gyamfi (thigh) and Mats Knoester (tendon), although all five are expected to return by the middle of next month.

Mantl; Brandon, McCarthy, Stranger, Schjonning-Larsen; Tshibola, Lowery; Kiltie, John-Jules, Owen; Hugill

Muller; Guinness-Walker, Happe, Milne, Devlin; Afeez, Lyons; Yogane, Ronan, Mahou; Nisbet

A new manager often brings fresh energy to a team, and that could provide Aberdeen with the much-needed impetus to avoid a fifth consecutive defeat. The Dons are unbeaten in their last three meetings with Killie, and we back them to preserve that record in this crucial encounter.

#2197. Graham Alexander set for Preston North End January overhaul with loan deals poised to be cancelled

Preston North End have had a disastrous season so far which has left them rock bottom of the Championship after 15 games. PNE are already seven points adrift of safety, with a managerial change to Graham Alexander so far not working out.

That leaves them in need of major changes in January, and Alexander is looking to make his mark on the squad. According to Pete O’Rourke, the Preston boss is hoping to terminate all his sides loan deals to replace them with his own targets in the winter.

North End currently have four loanees in their squad; Caleb Wiley, Liam Gibbs, Delano Burgzorg and Jusef Erabi. PNE have already brought in Greg Docherty under Alexander but he is clearly far from done with his Preston squad overhaul.

So far this season all of the PNE loanees have underperformed, which is evident in the Championship table. Erabi has managed just two goals in 15 appearances, while Burgzorg is yet to score despite contributing a handful of assists.

Wiley has shown promise, scoring on his Deepdale debut against Bristol City, but injury has restricted him to five appearances. Gibbs has also struggled for availability, making five appearances before suffering a quad injury that is expected to sideline him for several months.

Returning the four players in January would free up squad places and potentially allow Alexander to recruit players better suited to his preferred system. With the relegation battle intensifying, the manager needs greater reliability and quality from his available options.

Preston North End need to revamp their squad in January. They need something special to turn their season around after what has been a horrendous opening third of the campaign and returning those loanees is a simple way to switch things up.

However, with that said, PNE still need those loanees for another 10 games at least. With the busy festive period coming up, for those players to know that they are not wanted by Alexander might not be ideal.

He needs those players to give them all over the next months or so. Sometimes that can be a wake-up call for some players, who will see this as a time to prove themselves but it can also go in the other way.

PNE have a massive few weeks ahead which include the current loanees, which starts at West Ham this weekend. If Preston cant pickup some points in over December, they are going to be in major trouble no matter what happens in January.

#2196. Lazio vs Lecce - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 15:34, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:40

Surprise Serie A leaders Lazio will welcome Lecce to Stadio Olimpico on Saturday afternoon, aiming to extend their advantage at the top.

Yet to taste defeat in the league, the Biancocelesti sit one point above reigning champions Inter Milan, while their visitors are hovering above the drop zone.

Lazio left for the international break as top dogs in Serie A - which few would have predicted when they were dumped out of the Coppa Italia in August - and fans may even be dreaming of a first Scudetto for 27 years.

Under the guidance of Gennaro Gattuso, the Bianconcelesti have amassed 29 points from 11 top-flight games, setting a new club record.

Remarkably, that tally is 14 more than they had at this stage last term, and it leaves them one clear of second-placed Inter and two above city rivals Roma.

Gattuso’s side had to fight hard for a draw against Napoli last time out, having started strongly through Davide Frattesi's latest goal before conceding, then hanging on to avoid their first league defeat of the season.

While that ended a streak of six consecutive wins, Lazio will now aim to start a similar run ahead of next month’s Derby della Capitale, in which top spot could even be at stake.

First up is a visit from Lecce, to whom they have lost just twice in 19 Serie A home fixtures while averaging above two goals per game.

One of those defeats cost Lazio European qualification, as Lecce surprisingly prevailed on the final day of the 2024-25 season, but the Salentini only took one point from two meetings last term while failing to score.

For several months now, goals have been hard to come by, and Lecce are among Serie A’s lowest scorers once again.

A distinct lack of threat was apparent as Eusebio Di Francesco’s side lost three of their last four games before the break, only finding the net three times along the way.

After narrowly avoiding relegation last season, the Giallorossi surely face another survival fight in the coming months, having slipped to within three points of the drop zone.

Nonetheless, a recent 1-1 draw at Torino gives them something to build on, and - dating back to last term - Lecce have lost just three of their last nine away games.

With only the league to consider, Gattuso has made relatively few changes so far, and it should be a familiar Lazio XI that takes to the field this weekend.

However, the absence of Nuno Tavares and captain Mattia Zaccagni could see Alfonso Pedraza and Tijjani Noslin filling in on the left flank - often deployed up front, the latter has eight Serie A goal involvements this term.

Josip Sutalo is also injured, but fit-again pair Albert Gudmundsson and Nicolo Rovella are likely to start on the bench.

Italy midfielder Frattesi and Denmark winger Gustav Isaksen both scored in the UEFA Nations League, and they each have four league goals to their name this season.

By contrast, Lecce have struggled to find regular scorers. Only midfielder Lassana Coulibaly and centre-back Tiago Gabriel have found the net more than once, with forwards such as Willem Geubbels, Nikola Stulic and Paco Esteban all failing to fire.

In the treatment room, Joel Monteiro has yet to recover from a calf injury, while Santiago Pierotti and Ivan Ilic are not due back until next year.

Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Leite, Provstgaard, Pedraza; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin

Falcone; Veiga, Gabriel, Gaspar, Gallo; Coulibaly, Ngom, Maleh; N'Dri, Geubbels, Fatah

Though a fan boycott slightly negates Lazio's home advantage, they can comfortably claim a 10th league victory of the season.

Lecce's last success dates back to mid-October - against rock-bottom Udinese - and their wait for a win will go on.

#2194. Team news: 5 players set to miss Stoke City vs Birmingham City

The Championship is back after yet another international break, and we've now got a straight sprint until the Easter weekend with no interruptions.

The second-tier returns with a bang, as two of the sides sitting on 29 points atop the table go head-to-head at the bet365 Stadium on Saturday.

Stoke City, who have exceeded early-season expectations once more, will be keen not to fade away over the coming months like they did last year. A win at home against the current table-toppers, Birmingham City, would go a long way towards doing that.

The Blues were ruthless over the seven-game block between international breaks, winning six of seven, and three of those wins came by at least a three-goal margin. Their form away from St Andrew's is as big a contributor to their place atop the table, winning just one game fewer already this year than they did in the entirety of last season.

But only Swansea City and Middlesbrough — two fellow quick-starters — have come away from Stoke with all three points, and Kim Hellberg's side needed a late winner to do so. This won't be an easy matchup for either, and three points will give a massive boost to both sides' promotion hopes.

These five players, however, won't be able to feature.

French attacker Lamine Cisse had started six straight for Stoke before he went down inside 20 minutes against Bristol City last month and was forced off.

The extended run in the team, plus a goal in the win at Bolton Wanderers, gave hope that the £2m arrival last summer from Bastia was starting to find his feet in Mark Robins' side, so this setback is especially frustrating.

The ankle injury he picked up should see him out until Christmas.

Ato Ampah has had a terrible time with injuries ever since he arrived at Stoke from Chelsea's academy back in January.

He's yet to make his debut for the Potters due to a series of setbacks. Last season, it was an elongated recovery from a toe injury which kept him on the sidelines, and over pre-season he suffered a setback to that recovery.

While spending time with the Under-21s, though, the 20-year-old picked up an impact injury to his knee, which required surgery and will keep him out for the foreseeable future.

It's still unconfirmed whether Eric Bocat will be able to return against Birmingham. He's missed the last four games with a knee injury, which forced him off against Derby County last month.

FLW have reeled off some of the second tier's performers who are so easy on the eye

The hope after his diagnosis was that the left-back could make his return after the international break, but he remains a doubt, with Ben Johnson and Luca Bombino waiting in the wings to deputise in his absence.

Fellow left-back Aaron Cresswell is also a doubt for Saturday's clash with Birmingham, as he nears closer to a return to fitness from a knee injury he picked up in pre-season.

The 36-year-old remained a Stoke player over the summer, signing a one-year extension after he made 25 league appearances in his debut campaign following his departure from West Ham United.

Who do you think will come out on top between Stoke City and Birmingham City on Saturday? Let us know in the comments.

Birmingham's bill of health is relatively clear heading into the weekend. James Beadle and August Priske are both available again after missing a couple before the break, and Kristoffer Lund, who missed six weeks, is also back training.

Marc Leonard looked to be on his way out of Birmingham after heading on loan to Hearts back in January, but an Achilles injury suffered weeks before the end of the campaign saw him return to St Andrew's for treatment.

He'll remain out until the New Year, and all eyes will be on what his role in Chris Davies' side will be after his return.

#2193. Strasbourg vs Brest - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 19 Nov 2026 15:48

Vitor Matos takes charge of his first game at Strasbourg on Saturday when Brest visit the Stade de la Meinau, with the hosts looking to revive their season after a disappointing run of form prior to the international break.

The Alsace hosts sit 13th in the Ligue 1 table with 10 points from as many matches, just two clear of the relegation zone and five behind this weekend's opponents, who are themselves two points adrift of sixth-placed Nice.

Strasbourg head into Saturday's encounter having lost five of their last six league matches, with their only victory during that spell coming in an emphatic 5-1 home triumph over Auxerre on November 1.

While that result provided a brief respite following defeats to Paris FC, Nice and Paris Saint-Germain, Le Racing were unable to build on that success before the international break, going down 3-1 away to Toulouse on November 6.

That setback left Strasbourg with six defeats from their opening 10 league fixtures, scoring 18 times, while conceding 22 at the other end leaves the Alasce side with the second-worst defensive record among teams outside the bottom three, with at least three goals shipped in four separate matches.

Defensive frailties have been particularly evident on the road, where the Alsatian side have lost five of six league outings and conceded 16 goals, with a 6-2 victory over Troyes in early September accounting for their only away win during that spell.

However, Strasbourg have been considerably more competitive at the Stade de la Meinau, where they have picked up seven points from four games (W2, D1, L1) this term, and home advantage could prove valuable as the club looks to make a fresh start.

Saturday's fixture also marks the beginning of Matos's tenure following the club's decision to part company with Hugo Oliveira on Wednesday, with the former becoming Le Racing’s fourth head coach in less than a year after the departures of Liam Rosenior and Gary O'Neil.

Brest will be looking to maintain their momentum after signing off before the international break with consecutive 2-0 victories over Lorient and Lyon, recording back-to-back league wins for the first time this season and since three straight triumphs between late February and March.

Julien Lachuer's side have now won four of their opening 10 Ligue 1 fixtures (D3, L3) and have shown a reasonable balance at both ends of the pitch, conceding 12 goals while their tally of 18 scored is bettered only by Rennes (21) among teams outside the top six.

The Pirates have also been relatively consistent away from home, picking up eight points from five league trips through two wins, two draws and one defeat, with Auxerre responsible for their only setback on the road.

Furthermore, Brest have enjoyed considerable success on recent visits to Strasbourg, winning three of the last four encounters and drawing the other, while keeping clean sheets in three of those matches.

However, the visitors will be mindful of their most recent encounter, which ended in a 2-1 defeat when both sides met in Brest in May.

Strasbourg are waiting to assess Filip Jorgensen after the goalkeeper withdrew from Denmark duty with a minor injury, while Giovanni Reyna remains doubtful after missing international commitments following a thigh problem against Toulouse.

Joaquin Panichelli continues to recover from a torn anterior cruciate ligament and Fabio Balde is also doubtful after missing the last three club fixtures with a muscle injury.

Meanwhile, Jeyland Mitchell could miss a second consecutive match due to a fitness issue, while Maxi Oyedele has been sidelined since August and has yet to feature this season.

Gessime Yassine leads Strasbourg's scoring charts with four league goals and is expected to retain his place on the right flank after limited involvement with the Morocco national team during the international break.

Brest will once again look to Ludovic Ajorque to lead the attacking line, with the French forward having scored five goals this term, while Kamory Doumbia, who has found the net four times this campaign, is expected to provide support in the number 10 role.

#2192. Bolton Wanderers dodged a transfer bullet in walking away from £3m striker pursuit amid new blow: Opinion

On Deadline Day, both Bolton Wanderers and Preston North End were in the market for a striker. At the last hour, Celtic striker Johnny Kenny, who had spent the second half of the season prior at the Trotters, was made available.

Steven Schumacher‘s side would make a move for the 23-year-old, but Celtic’s price tag and PNE’s £3m offer would see BWFC walk away from a deal. And, Republic of Ireland international Kenny duly made the move to Deepdale.

Now though, according to The Lancashire Post’s Dan Murphy, Kenny is now out for the next couple of months with a hamstring injury. The striker’s injury struggles have meant that, in hindsight, Bolton Wanderers were better off looking elsewhere.

At the start of summer, Schumacher made it clear he’d welcome back a number of Bolton Wanderers loan stars, including Johnny Kenny. However, BWFC would not have the same spending power they had in League One, and being frugal with their budget would be at the top of the priority list.

The Trotters made 13 signings and Kenny would have been their marquee addition of the summer. The 23-year-old scored six goals, with a total of nine goal involvements in his time with the Trotters. In the end, the £3m price tag put Wanderers off, and they look right to have walked away.

Kenny has two goals so far for Preston North End but has played just eight games, having also suffered an injury that made him miss the play-offs with BWFC. The North West outfit would not have been able to bring in as many players if they had signed the forward, and so far they are nine points above their Lancashire rivals.

So far, Kenny has missed three games for the Lilywhites and could now miss at least the next 15 as he recovers from his new hamstring injury. The striker was one of Preston North End’s big signings, and with both them and Bolton Wanderers in a relegation fight, it is easy to see which team is in a better position after their summer recruitment.

For the Trotters, £3m is a lot of money, if not all their transfer budget, and it looks like they’ve dodged a serious problem by walking away from the deal.

Theo Bair, who signed the same day as Kenny joined PNE, has three goal involvements whilst Sam Dalby has six goals, sitting sixth in the Championship goalscoring charts. BWFC may still need more firepower at the top of the pitch, but they also need players on the pitch, and right now their double act is doing just that, whilst Kenny remains sidelined.

#2191. Team news: 8 players set to miss Wolves vs Charlton Athletic

The Championship returns this weekend after the November international break, and at Molineux, Wolves look to extend their unbeaten league run to seven against Charlton Athletic.

The Addicks picked up a much-needed 2-1 win over Sheffield United at the Valley in the final game before the break, snapping an 11-game winless streak and alleviating some of the pressure that may have been building on Nathan Jones.

Now the next task is to replicate that on the road, where they've failed to win since their first away game of the season against West Ham United, but it won't be easy against a Wolves side who are within touching distance of top spot.

There are still parts of the Old Gold fanbase who are sceptical of head coach Cesar Peixoto, but one thing they can agree on is that, Bolton Wanderers aside, they've been well in control of their home games this season.

Both sides will be keen to take all three points, but these eight players won't be available to help do so.

The key injury in the Wolves camp remains with Raul Jimenez, with the veteran striker set to miss the rest of the calendar year after going in for knee surgery in mid-October.

The 35-year-old rejoined the club this past summer after three years at Fulham, where he still showcased his Premier League goalscoring qualities, netting 28 league goals in those three seasons.

He scored three in his first six back at Molineux, but isn't close to being able to add to that.

Left-back Ghislain Konan was brought to Wolves in the summer from Gil Vicente, reuniting with Cesar Peixoto in the first place. The 30-year-old provided some much-needed experience, with 59 Ivorian caps throughout his career.

However, Konan hasn't gotten going in the Old Gold just yet, and after just three appearances, he was sidelined until late December after picking up an MCL injury.

Charlton boss Nathan Jones was as coy as ever when discussing injuries ahead of the trip to Wolves, stating that those who missed Sheffield United are "closer than they were two weeks ago," and instead putting the focus on those who came in to replace those injured players.

Club captain Lloyd Jones was absent from a league squad for the first time this season against the Blades. He'd played every minute up until then. The hip injury he picked up could see him back this weekend, but he remains a doubt.

Karlarn Grant has also been a key part of Nathan Jones' side since making his return to the side he came through the academy with this past summer.

Nathaniel Chalobah was the third absentee from that win over Sheffield United after picking up a thigh injury.

It's the latest setback in what has been a troubling few years for the 31-year-old. He's already missed two months of the current season with a similar issue, and only played just over 1,000 minutes of league action across two years at Sheffield Wednesday prior to his summer move to the Valley, due to injury, too.

Reece Burke is another in the Charlton squad who has battled injury problems throughout his career. He reunited with ex-Luton Town boss Jones ahead of last season, having played fewer than 27 league games per year in his four campaigns with the Hatters.

He only managed 17 appearances last season and has yet to see the pitch this year after suffering an innocuous injury ahead of an EFL Cup match with Tottenham Hotspur back in August.

Charlton are more transparent with their long-term setbacks. Rob Apter is one of those, with a knee injury picked up a month ago, sidelining him for "an extended spell."

The Scotsman was on the fringes anyway, with just 11 Championship minutes under his belt. The former Blackpool man spent the latter stages of last season on loan at Bolton.

Kenyan centre-back Collins Sichenje will miss the remainder of the campaign after he suffered an ACL injury during that aforementioned EFL Cup tie at Tottenham back in August.

The 23-year-old has only made 10 appearances since his mid-season move from Vojvodina last term.

#2189. Rayo Vallecano vs Valencia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 15:50, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:53

Rayo Vallecano and Valencia will both be looking to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they resume their respective La Liga campaigns in Madrid on Saturday.

Valencia's last match at this level ended in a 3-0 reverse to Real Madrid, while Rayo were beaten 1-0 by Real Sociedad in their final fixture ahead of the November international break.

Rayo have a record of three wins, three draws and five defeats from their 11 league matches this season, with a total of 12 points leaving them in 14th spot in the La Liga table.

The capital outfit are currently six points off sixth-placed Sevilla and two points outside of the relegation zone, so it has been a mixed start to the campaign, and they have only managed to win one of their last five fixtures in Spain's top flight.

Benat San Jose's side have been impressive on home soil this season, picking up 10 points from five matches, but it has been a struggle for them on their travels, yet to record a win from six fixtures.

Los Franjirrojos, who finished eighth in Spain's top flight last season, have only managed to win 10 of their previous 52 matches against Valencia throughout history.

However, four of their last five contests have finished all square, including a 1-1 draw in the corresponding match between the two teams last season.

Valencia have not actually beaten Rayo since December 2023, while they have just two wins over the capital outfit in all competitions since December 2014.

Seven of the last 10 matches between these two teams have finished level, but Los Che will have their eyes on what would be just a third league win of the campaign.

A record of two wins, three draws and seven defeats from 12 matches has left Javier Aguirre's side down in 19th spot in the table, picking up just nine points.

Los Che suffered a 3-0 defeat to Real Madrid in their last league fixture, but they have been in action since, securing their spot in the second round of the Copa del Rey courtesy of a 6-0 victory over Tavernes on November 10.

Valencia have actually claimed seven of their nine league points this season on their travels, boasting a record of two wins, one draw and two defeats.

Rayo will again be missing Augusto Batalla through injury this weekend, while Alvaro Garcia, Marash Kumbulla, Luiz Felipe and Oscar Valentin could also be absent.

Sergio Camello has scored seven times in 12 league appearances during the 2026-27 campaign, and the 25-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There is also set to be a spot in the wide for Jorge de Frutos, while Pathe Ciss should continue in the middle of the midfield for the capital outfit.

As for Valencia, Jose Gaya is suspended following his red card against Real Madrid.

Sergi Canos is a long-term absentee due to a serious knee injury, while Diego Lopez and David Otorbi remain fitness doubts for the away side.

Umar Sadiq and Arnaut Danjuma are facing late fitness tests, but the expectation is that the duo will be available for selection on Saturday.

There will be changes to the side that started the game against Real Madrid, with Luis Rioja and Filip Ugrinic expected to be introduced into the XI.

#2188. EFL club officially confirm they're going to reduce capacity of their stadium

Mansfield Town have made a decision to decrease the capacity of the One Call Stadium, otherwise known as Field Mill, after a meeting with the Safety Advisory Group.

The Stags are currently in the midst of a third successive campaign in League One, with Nigel Clough's side amassing 19 points from 12 matches.

As a result of the club's recent trajectory, Mansfield have welcomed several fallen giants to this part of Nottinghamshire.

Stags fans have developed a reputation for generating plenty of noise, which, in turn, has led to a strong atmosphere with those backing the visiting sides housed in the stadium's North Stand.

However, the decision, which has been made ahead of Saturday's clash with MK Dons, hasn't gone down well with several fans.

The One Call Stadium is currently the fifth-smallest stadium in League One, with only the home grounds of Cambridge United, Stevenage, Burton Albion and Bromley able to house fewer spectators.

Attendances so far this season have been at the 8,527 mark on average, but Mansfield will now see fewer visiting supporters pass through the turnstiles.

A statement from Nottinghamshire Council on Friday confirmed that the stadium's North Stand will be reduced in capacity from 1,000 to 600 following incidents relating to crowd management and control in the EFL Trophy clash against Chesterfield, which the League Two side won 5-3.

Mansfield have since confirmed the agreement in conjunction with the council and Safety Advisory Group, but also confirmed that the club are exploring the possibility of a safe-standing area within the stand.

Although this decision doesn't have a major impact on the matchday experience of the home support at the One Call Stadium, other than the fact there are fewer visiting fans to engage in back-and-forth with, it has caused plenty of responses.

One Stags supporter wrote: "SAG vs Mansfield Town yet again. Do they ever work with the club rather than against it?"

"But why? What was said in the meeting? Away fans getting punished by the SAG which reflects on the club? They deserve a bit of clarity," another commented.

"Poor decision and tbh, it’s rarely full," backed up the feeling of confusion as to why such measures have been taken.

Another Mansfield fan debated: "Surely (has) to be done up and down the country then?

"There is literally nothing wrong with away fans standing up. SAG need to give their head a wobble," was one of many strong reactions.

With Mansfield's last two home games coming against the Spireites and Notts County, another questioned: "Did SAG not look at who the last 3 games have been against at home? At least 2 they should’ve known it would’ve been an issue."

One of the potential fans visiting from Buckinghamshire on Saturday said: "What('s) wrong with standing up? No need to close off part of the stand because of it."

What do you make of Mansfield Town's decision to reduce the One Call Stadium's capacity? Comment below!

However, a Port Vale fan agreed with the decision, replying: "The ticket regulations say that fans should be sitting down. If they stand up and refuse to sit then have them thrown out. If they refuse to leave then have police arrest them. Don't punish other fans because there are some idiots."

Although Mansfield clarified that the allocation will be temporarily reduced, it has already been debated for how long this will be the case.

Recent fixtures have clearly impacted this decision, and some of League One's largest fanbases could be left scrambling for tickets depending on how long such measures are in place.

Indeed, the Stags are still yet to host the likes of Barnsley, Sheffield Wednesday and Leicester City, with it not exactly being an arduous journey for those who follow the Tykes, Owls and Foxes to make.

FLW have ranked the 10 best EFL League One stadiums so far in the 2026/27 season, including Bradford City and Sheffield Wednesday.

Ironically, the decision to house fewer away supporters could still play to the advantage of Clough's side, who have picked up the majority of their points so far on home turf.

#2187. Southampton vs Derby County - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 15:52, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:54

Southampton will resume their Championship campaign with a home clash against Derby County on Saturday.

The Saints return from the international break in seventh spot, while the Rams are languishing in 23rd place in the Championship table.

Southampton enjoyed a fine run of form after returning from the September/October international break, recording four wins and two draws in a six-game unbeaten run.

However, their undefeated streak came to a disappointing end with a 1-0 away loss against basement side Preston North End in their final outing before the two-week break.

Tonda Eckert’s side failed to produce a response to Jordan Thompson’s 33rd-minute effort, as they drew a blank for the first time on the road this season.

Despite that result, the Saints are still firmly in the promotion battle, sitting in seventh spot and five points adrift of the automatic promotion places ahead of Saturday’s meeting with the Rams.

They head into that contest with the league’s best home record, having won six and drawn one of their seven Championship outings at St Mary’s this term, scoring 20 goals and conceding on just five occasions.

They have also won their last two home league games against Derby, including a hard-fought 2-1 victory in April’s encounter between the two sides.

While the Saints are targeting promotion, Derby are focusing on retaining their Championship status after winning just two of their 15 league matches (D4, L9).

They at least managed to end a 10-game winless run in their final outing before the international window, which saw them overturn a one-goal deficit to record a 3-1 victory over Bolton Wanderers.

Ryan Nyambe, Jack Robinson and Rhian Brewster all found the net in the second period to ease some of the heavy pressure on head coach John Eustace.

However, Eustace knows he needs a positive run of results if he is to prove he is the right manager to lead Derby out of their current predicament, with five points separating the Rams from safety.

Derby have failed to win any of their last five away games, but they have at least enjoyed success on the south coast this season, with September’s 2-0 win over Portsmouth representing their only win on the road this term.

If they are to claim the spoils on Saturday, the visitors will need to claim their first Championship win at St Mary’s since recording a 2-1 victory in the second leg of the 2006-07 playoff semi-finals.

Southampton defender Keven Schlotterbeck will be out for around six weeks after suffering a dislocated shoulder in the defeat to Preston.

The Saints will also have to assess their star forward Cyle Larin, who missed the last four games before the international window with a hamstring problem.

Midfielder Caspar Jander is another injury concern, having sat out the previous three matches with a muscular injury.

As for the Rams, Sammie Szmodics is expected to be out until mid-December after sustaining a knee injury in the loss to Norwich at the start of the month.

Derby are also without Craig Forsyth, Sondre Langas, Charlie Taylor and Derry Murkin for the trip to the south coast.

Eiran Cashin, Matt Clarke, Joe Ward, Ryan Hedges and Patrick Agyemang are closing in on making their respective returns from injury, although it remains to be seen whether any of the quintet will be ready for Saturday’s fixture.

#2186. Vitor Matos admits ‘anger’ expectation after leaving Swansea City to join Strasbourg

Swansea City confirmed on Wednesday that head coach Vitor Matos had left the club to take charge of Strasbourg, with the Portuguese manager’s appointment officially announced. The Swans received compensation of around £5m, with Leon Britton and Kris O’Leary taking charge on an interim basis, alongside former defender Ashley Williams.

Matos’ departure came as a shock and it has left sour feelings from Swansea City fans. Speaking ahead of his first game as Strasbourg boss, Matos has revealed his feelings towards his former side, and what he expects from the Swansea fans.

As reported by French news outlet ICI Alsace, Matos said: “It was a difficult decision to leave Swansea. I expect nothing from the fans but anger, and I understand it“.

He added:“It’s a really exciting project and I felt I could help move the team forward. It wasn’t an easy decision to leave Swansea, given the emotional dimension and emotional bonds I had forged there.”

It does not seem a replacement for Matos is close with Britton, O’Leary and Williams in charge for the clash against West Brom. Rob Edwards and Tommy Elphick are reportedly on the clubs radar as potentially replacements.

Swansea City will be frustrated to lose another manager just as they appeared to be building towards something special. The situation is reminiscent of Russell Martin’s departure, when he was poached by Southampton.

The Swans made significant progress under Matos, so finding a successor who can maintain a similar tactical approach should be a priority. Doing so would allow them to get the best out of the existing squad while limiting the disruption and adjustment period that inevitably comes with an unexpected change in the dugout.

Swansea City will be carefully weighing up a number of candidates, but there will be an urgency to appoint Matos’ replacement as quickly and efficiently as possible. The longer the vacancy remains, the greater the risk of disrupting the momentum they had begun to build.

Swansea City took a bold gamble when appointing Matos last season. He arrived with very little experience as a head coach, but the decision has proved to be an inspired one and could earn the club a substantial compensation fee at the very least.

With his departure looking increasingly likely amid his interest in the Strasbourg job, the Swans should have plenty of confidence in their ability to find a suitable replacement. The Matos appointment itself is evidence of their judgement, while their recent transfer windows have also been particularly impressive.

Overall, Swansea’s recruitment of both players and staff has been very strong and has helped transform them into a much more competitive side. There is little reason to doubt that their next managerial appointment could be another success.

#2185. Middlesbrough vs Bristol City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 15:53, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:00

Middlesbrough will be looking to move to the top of the Championship table this weekend when they welcome a struggling Bristol City side to the Riverside Stadium.

Boro entered the final international break of the year having missed the opportunity to become league leaders, as a defeat to Wrexham was followed by a goalless draw away to Watford, while the Robins continued their slide down the table after suffering a humiliating 5-0 home defeat to Norwich City just under a fortnight ago.

Kim Hellberg and his Middlesbrough side return to the Riverside Stadium for the first time since Halloween with an opportunity to leapfrog Birmingham City and move to the top of the Championship table.

The Blues have made an unexpected push for first place in recent weeks after winning three consecutive matches, while Boro managed just one victory, alongside a defeat and a draw, leaving both sides level on 29 points ahead of matchweek 16.

Such is the competitiveness of the Championship that Middlesbrough's tally of 29 points provides them with just a three-point cushion over sixth place, highlighting how quickly the standings can change.

Although their form at the start of November was somewhat inconsistent, Boro return to home soil where they are unbeaten in seven matches, collecting 17 points and scoring 17 goals during that run, with only Southampton boasting a better home record than Hellberg's side.

Last season saw Hellberg and his Middlesbrough team miss out on promotion to the Premier League following one of the most dramatic and controversial playoff campaigns in recent memory, despite occupying a place in the top two for much of the season.

Their success during the 2025-26 campaign was built on a prolific attack that scored 72 goals in 46 matches, a total bettered by just three teams, and they have once again impressed in the final third this season, with only one side scoring more than their 30 goals.

As for Bristol City, they entered the international break with serious questions surrounding the future of manager Michael Skubala after a dreadful run of form saw them fall out of the playoff places and down to 17th in the table.

Since the first international break ended in September, the Robins have won just one of their subsequent seven Championship matches and were widely tipped to part company with the former Lincoln City boss during the past fortnight, but the club have opted to stick with him as he prepares to take charge of his 17th match on Saturday.

A short video published by the club last week showed CEO Charlie Boss confirming that they would "give Skubala the opportunity to turn around the home form", with Bristol City's two victories at Ashton Gate representing the fourth-worst record in the division and a stark contrast to that of their upcoming opponents.

The Robins enjoyed a productive seven-day spell in which they collected nine points from a possible nine against Portsmouth, Preston North End and Burnley, but have since suffered a series of disappointing results that have seen their playoff ambitions replaced by growing concerns over a potential relegation battle.

Norwich arrived in the South West in encouraging form, but few would have expected them to inflict such a heavy defeat on Skubala's side, with the 5-0 loss at Ashton Gate subsequently described by the manager as one of the most difficult afternoons of his career.

Although the Robins face one of the division's strongest sides this weekend, they can at least take confidence from their recent record against Boro, with the North Yorkshire outfit winless in their last nine league meetings and without a victory over Bristol City since August 2021.

Middlesbrough could name the same starting XI that drew with Watford almost a fortnight ago, although Hellberg may be tempted to make changes as his side look to return to winning ways.

Former Robins goalkeeper Radek Vitek is expected to retain his place between the posts, while former Bristol City players Tommy Conway, Neto Borges and Luke Ayling could all come into contention to face their old club after starting on the bench last time out.

Rokas Pusktas has suffered another injury setback after undergoing surgery on a hamstring problem and has managed just 12 minutes of football for Boro since joining from Hajduk Split in August.

Hellberg will also be without Alfie Jones, who remains sidelined with a calf injury, but could welcome the Championship's leading scorer back into the fold, with Will Lankshear looking to add to his 13 league goals, which have come at an impressive rate of one every 81 minutes.

Meanwhile, Bristol City are expected to have just one absentee for Saturday's trip north, with Noah Eile likely to miss out through illness.

Although their major injury crisis from last season is very much a thing of the past, the Robins have made several unexpected changes to their recent starting lineups, making it difficult to predict the team Skubala will select.

New goalkeeper Sam Tickle was dropped in favour of Brad Collins after just 11 appearances for his new club but could be reinstated after his replacement made several high-profile errors leading to goals during his four starts, conceding an average of 2.3 goals per game during that time.

Skubala has also alternated between a lone striker and a two-man forward partnership in recent weeks and could once again make changes as he looks to turn around his side's disappointing run of form.

Rio Cardines opted out of international duty with Trinidad and Tobago over the past fortnight after featuring in every one of the Robins' Championship matches during his debut season as a professional, and he is expected to return to the attack this weekend as he looks to build on the impressive six assists he has already provided.

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Bryam; Berhalter, Morris, McGree; Conway, Strelec, Sarmiento

Tickle; Tanner, Dickie, Eissat, Pring; Williams, Randell; Cardines, Knight, Twine; Tolaj

With one of the division's most out-of-form sides facing a team that has been exceptionally difficult to beat on home soil, we expect the result to go Middlesbrough's way.

Although the Robins boast an impressive recent record against Boro, we expect that run to come to an end on Saturday as Hellberg's side continue their push towards the top of the Championship table.

#2184. Moreira discusses first Belgium goal, ‘special’ Milan group and learning in Italy: “I’ll always remember”

Last night, Diego Moreira scored his first goal for Belgium and AC Milan will be very happy to see their investment continuing to shine.

It’s fair to say that Moreira has been a revelation for Milan. His arrival came out of nowhere, with a deal first reported by FootballKush and then it was picked up by the biggest sources in football. His first appearance was a struggle against Juventus, but the rest, as they say, is history.

Goals have come regularly, with huge appearances that have defined the Rossoneri’s season already. For example, the goal against Inter, with two assists to accompany it. He’s perhaps been the signing of the season in Italy and there’d maybe be a conversation about Europe, too.

After scoring against Italy, Moreira spoke to Sky, looking at the team’s performance, playing with Kevin De Bruyne and the feeling of grabbing his first goal for his country, as MilanNews relays.

“I’m very happy with my first goal for the national team. It was a special moment because my family was there. It’s a day I’ll always remember.”

Mancini said that you deserved to win and that you are a very strong team…

“We have some very strong players up front, like Doku, De Bruyne, but I think that in the end it’s a sport where everyone is needed and we all played a great game.”

What does it mean to play with a player like De Bruyne?

“De Bruyne is special; it’s a pleasure to have him with us because he sees things that others don’t see, he has a lot of experience and we’re happy to have him in our team.”

What do you take from this experience with the national team at AC Milan?

“I learned a lot in Italy because it’s a league with a lot of experienced players. Playing for the national team and for AC Milan are two very positive things, and I’m very happy.”

How do you recover in Europe after a difficult start?

“It’s difficult but we’re working towards this. We have to be prepared and we have players who will help us with this.”

Then, in the mixed zone, he was also intercepted by MilanNews, where he also answered a few questions about the Rossoneri.

Diego, you scored in your first Milan derby, just like Kaká, Shevchenko, and Ronaldinho before you. How have you settled in at AC Milan?

“I’m very happy. At AC Milan, I’m surrounded by a special group, with many great players. Having them around me helps me a lot, especially in terms of experience. It’s true, the match against Inter was special. I’ll continue to work hard and give my best.”

Good in Serie A, bad in the Europa League: why this two-faced Milan?

“I’m on the national team right now, and you’re asking me about Milan?”

Belgium practically overwhelmed Italy, your current footballing nation. It ended 4-1, but the scoreline could have been eight or nine goals…

“It’s something special, and we’re very happy. It was an important match, so winning and scoring was really nice.”

#2183. Barnsley make Huddersfield Town ticket announcement and it's caused backlash

Barnsley have confirmed that adult tickets for their game against Huddersfield Town next month will cost £35.

The Tykes have had a tough season so far, with Daniel Stendel’s return to Oakwell not producing the results that many had hoped, as the team sit in the relegation zone.

However, many fans recognise that Barnsley’s problems run deeper right now, and there are calls for the owners to leave the club.

Whilst the criticism towards those at the top of the club is wide-ranging, one aspect that has left fans annoyed is the price it costs to watch games.

And, that has ignited again, with the club confirming that adult tickets for the home clash against Huddersfield on December 19 will be £35.

This was always going to be a game that was priced higher than most, as there is a rivalry between the two Yorkshire clubs - and it’s worth noting it’s the same pricing structure as the one they went with against Sheffield Wednesday.

Plus, with Huddersfield flying high, they are likely to shift a lot of tickets, so Barnsley, who will be charging the visitors £35 as well, will see this as a chance to make money.

Firstly, it should be said that problems with ticket prices are not exclusive to Barnsley, and fans of clubs up and down the country would want their own clubs to review prices.

But, in this instance, you can understand why Barnsley fans are furious, as £35 is an awful lot of money to watch a League One fixture.

Barnsley will be wincing at the latest news out of League One involving Bradford and a potential takeover development mirroring Sheffield Wednesday's.

Yes, it’s a game against a local side, but Barnsley are battling to stay in the third tier right now, so they should be doing all they can to bring supporters back, which isn’t going to happen when you’re charging £35.

Plus, this is a game that will be played a week before Christmas, at a time when money is tight for everyone. When you combine that with the fixture being televised, it really is a poor decision from Barnsley, who are prioritising money over fans.

Again, they’re by no means the only club to do that, but it’s a shame that they aren’t going the other way and trying to do affordable deals to entice supporters back.

Of course, the hierarchy will argue that they need to bring in funds to help the club, but it’s always about striking the right balance and making fans feel valued.

What do you make of Barnsley's ticket prices? Let us know in the comments below.

As you would expect, this development didn’t go down well with the Barnsley fans, with many making it clear that they feel this is far too much money to ask fans to pay.

However, there was one Barnsley fan who did understand the thinking of the Barnsley hierarchy, as he explained why it made 'commercial sense'.

Meanwhile, these Huddersfield fans couldn't resist having a dig at their rivals, as they joked that £35 was more than fair to get to watch Martin Drury's team, and one player in particular.

#2182. Chelsea vs Leeds United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:24

Chelsea will be looking to return to winning ways and strengthen their top-four credentials when they take on Leeds United in Saturday afternoon’s Premier League contest at Stamford Bridge.

These two teams served up a nine-goal thriller in the EFL Cup just a couple of months ago, with the West Londoners securing a 6-3 comeback victory in the third round.

Chelsea entered the international break on a sour note with just one win and three defeats to their name in all competitions, crashing out of the EFL Cup to Liverpool and enduring two setbacks in the Premier League.

The Blues responded to a surprise 2-0 home loss to Spurs by beating Man United at Stamford Bridge by the same scoreline, but they came back down to earth a fortnight ago with a disappointing 1-0 defeat to basement club Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

Five wins, one draw and four defeats have been posted in Xabi Alonso’s first 10 top-flight games for Chelsea, who sit fifth in the Premier League table and just two points behind Liverpool in fourth. However, Aston Villa down in 10th spot are only three points adrift of the Blues.

Having lost three of their first five PL away games for the first time since 2015-16 under Jose Mourinho, Chelsea should welcome this weekend’s return to Stamford Bridge where they have accumulated 10 of their 16 top-flight points this term, scoring the second-most home goals in the division (13).

The West Londoners have also won eight of their last 10 home battles with Leeds across all tournaments (D2) since a 2-0 defeat back in December 1999, though they were held to a 2-2 draw in this exact league fixture last season after letting a two-goal lead slip in the second half.

Following a five-match winless run that placed Daniel Farke under growing pressure, Leeds secured a much-needed 1-0 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road to enter the international break on a high.

A dominant second-half display was rewarded with a late strike from substitute Noah Okafor to help Leeds claim their third Premier League win of the season and rise to ninth in the table, six points clear of the bottom three and just two points behind Saturday’s opponents Chelsea in fifth.

Leeds are unbeaten across their last nine Premier League home matches (W5 D4) – their longest run at Elland Road in the top flight since an impressive 15-match streak between January and December 2001 – but they have only won one of their last eight league games on the road (D4 L3).

The Whites are now gearing up for four tricky away trips to Chelsea, Man City, Liverpool and Aston Villa, with Farke hoping that his side can showcase the same relentless character, commitment and unity shown in their win over Spurs as they attempt to improve their fortunes away from home.

Leeds head into this weekend’s contest seeking to end a 10-game winless run away against Chelsea in all competitions (D2 L8). However, having avoided defeat in their last two league meetings (3-1 at home, 2-2 away), the Whites will aim to go three consecutive games unbeaten against the Blues for the first time since between November 2000 and October 2001.

Chelsea quintet Joao Pedro (thigh), Jorrel Hato (back), Reece James (knee), Maxence Lacroix (hamstring) and Jamie Gittens (ankle) all remain sidelined with injuries.

However, Moises Caicedo (illness) and Josh Acheampong (unspecified) are both available for selection, while goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is also ready to start ahead for Mike Penders after recovering from a broken jaw to represent Argentina during the international break.

Morgan Rogers provided four second-half assists in the aforementioned EFL Cup win over Leeds in September, while Cole Palmer and Danny Welbeck both netted a brace. However, Welbeck may have to settle for a place on the bench once again, with Alonso possibly favouring either Estevao Willian or Pedro Neto in a central role alongside Rogers and Palmer.

As for Leeds, young forward Mateo Joseph is making positive progress in his recovery from a serious knee injury, but he remains sidelined, while midfielder Anton Stach is doubtful after missing the win over Spurs with a broken toe.

Farke will consider sticking with a two-man frontline of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha, with Sean Longstaff and Ao Tanaka linking up with ex-Chelsea youngster Ethan Ampadu in midfield.

However, Noah Okafor will hope to force his way into the first XI after scoring as a substitute against Spurs, while Harry Wilson, Brendan Aaronson and Joe Rodon are also contenders to earn a recall, the latter of whom recently recovered from a long-term injury.

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill; Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Palestra; Estevao, Rogers, Palmer

Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Tanaka, Ampadu, Gudmundsson; Wilson, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin

Chelsea have not been the same prolific outfit without the presence of Joao Pedro up front, and they could find it difficult to break down a robust Leeds backline without a natural focal point.

Despite only one of the Blues' last six Premier League matches seeing both teams score, we can see the net rippling at both ends on this occasion, with the hosts bouncing back from recent setbacks and edging to a slender victory.

#2181. The West Ham teenager who stunned Arsenal is back after four years

Former West Ham United midfielder Reece Oxford has returned to English football, as he signed a deal with League One side, Bromley.

The midfielder first caught the eye with the Hammers in the early stages of his professional career, as he produced an eye-catching display in his senior debut against Arsenal in August 2015.

Oxford became West Ham's youngest-ever Premier League player at 16 years and 236 days old, and his performance looked as though he'd been playing regularly in the top-flight.

West Ham ran out 2-0 winners at the Emirates against Arsenal in that match, and Oxford came in for high praise from Sky Sports' co-commentator on the day, Niall Quinn.

“He’s been phenomenal. A star is born,” Sky Sports co-commentator Niall Quinn said. “He’s been mature, he’s ordering people around. It’s unbelievable to see. He’s mobile, he gets around and he knows the game. He’s a natural.”

Oxford went on to label his performance as a 'dream debut' in the win over the Gunners, and an 'honour' to play for West Ham in the top-flight.

“It was a dream debut,” Oxford told Sky Sports. “It’s an honour to play for West Ham and to be the youngest.”

Oxford is now 27-years-old, and it's fair to say that his career hasn't quite hit the heights that he and supporters would have originally hoped to see.

Whilst contracted to West Ham, he had loan spells with Reading whilst they were in the Championship, before two brief spells with German side Borussia Mönchengladbach, before having his final loan spell with FC Augsburg.

He seemingly made a good impression with Augsburg as well, as he went on to sign for them on a permanent basis in 2019. Oxford then spent six years in Germany with them, making 80 appearances in total across all competitions.

The former England youth international's time with Augsburg came to an end at the end of the 2024/25 season, when he departed when his contracted expired.

Can you see Reece Oxford's move to Bromley kickstarting his career again? Let us know in the comments!

The midfielder had a year out of competitive football, and it'll be interesting to see if he can recapture his best form, as he's a player with real quality when at his best, which we saw with both West Ham and Augsburg.

There will be some doubts whether he can do that though, as Oxford hasn't played a competitive match since November 2022, as he's had numerous injury problems which have stalled his development in senior football.

A move to Bromley could be the ideal move for him, although the League One side are struggling in their efforts to avoid relegation back into League Two.

Bromley are next in action on Saturday, when they travel to the Select Car Leasing Stadium to take on Reading, in what will be Oxford's first trip back to his former club.

Bromley have found it tough to build any sort of momentum this season, as they're bottom of the League One table, as well as being three points adrift of safety heading into this weekend's fixtures.

This dismal run of form includes being winless from their last 11 matches, and it's a tough ask for them to end that run against a Reading side that have only lost once at home so far in the 2026/27 season.

Oxford has a point to prove at this level, having not played this far down the English football pyramid, but if he can hit the ground running, then Bromley will have a great player on their hands.

#2180. Lille vs Lyon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 19 Nov 2026 16:04, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:37

Lille will be looking to strengthen their position in the Ligue 1 title race when they welcome Lyon to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Saturday evening for matchday 11 action.

The hosts sit second in the Ligue 1 table with 21 points from their opening 10 matches, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain, while the fifth-placed visitors have 17 points and will be hoping to close the gap on their opponents in Carlos Vicens's first game in charge.

Lille head into the weekend in encouraging form after winning their last two league outings, beating Lens 1-0 before claiming a 2-1 victory away to Rennes prior to the international break, where Nathan Ngoy's second-half goal proved decisive.

Davide Ancelotti will be particularly pleased with how his side have rediscovered their rhythm after consecutive draws against Brest and Monaco derailed the Mastiffs' title charge, with the northern French outfit having lost just once in their opening 10 Ligue 1 fixtures (W6, D3).

Much of Lille's success this season has been built on their defensive solidity, with seven goals conceded representing the best record in the division, while five clean sheets leave them behind only Lorient (six) in that regard.

Les Dogues have also found the net in every league outing this season, although they have scored more than once in just 40% of their 10 top-flight matches, including two of their five fixtures on their own turf.

Nevertheless, Lille have been reliable at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy, winning three of their five Ligue 1 games at the ground and avoiding defeat in the other two to boast the division's fifth-best home record.

Victory on Saturday would not only strengthen the hosts' position in the standings but also provide a timely confidence boost ahead of Wednesday's Champions League meeting with Bayern Munich, with the Mastiffs currently second from bottom in the league phase table after collecting just one point from their opening four continental fixtures.

Vicens will also have one eye on next Thursday’s home meeting with Lillstrom in the Europa League, where Lyon sit 13th in the 36-team table after picking up seven points from their first four matches.

However, the Spanish coach's immediate priority will be to get his new side back to winning ways following a 2-0 defeat at Brest in Lyon's most recent league outing, which came under interim boss Jorge Maciel following the departure of Paolo Fonseca for Sporting Lisbon.

That setback further highlighted Lyon's struggles on the road, having now lost their last three Ligue 1 away matches while conceding exactly two goals in each of those outings, with their only victory in five domestic trips this season coming against Toulouse on the opening weekend.

Nevertheless, a superior head-to-head record should offer the visitors some encouragement ahead of Saturday's contest, considering Lyon have won six of their last seven meetings across all competitions (D1) with Lille, including 1-0 victories in both league encounters last season.

Lille remain without Tiago Santos, who is expected to miss the remainder of the season after rupturing his cruciate ligament, while Hamza Igamane is also unavailable as he continues his recovery from an ACL injury, although a return is expected in December.

Ayase Ueda is doubtful after sustaining a plantar fascia injury, with the forward having resumed running but yet to return to full training, although Ancelotti previously suggested that the Japanese attacker could be available for this fixture.

Hakon Arnar Haraldsson has operated as a makeshift centre-forward in Ueda's absence and could continue in that position if the latter fails to recover in time, although veteran striker Olivier Giroud also provides an alternative.

Meanwhile, Lyon will be without Tyler Morton, who recently underwent surgery for an abductor problem, while Pavel Sulc is recovering from a meniscus injury and Mohamed Ouedraogo is sidelined for the remainder of the campaign after rupturing his cruciate ligament.

Lois Openda also remains unavailable as he recovers from a fractured fibula, although the forward is expected to return in the coming weeks, while Steeve Kango could be available after rejoining group training following a period under concussion protocol.

Ozer; Ngoy, Nianzou, Alexsandro, Perraud; Bentaleb, Andre, Mukau; E Mbappe, Haraldsson, Diaoune

Greif; Athekame, Niakhate, Bacher, A Vinicius; Tessmann, Bidstrup, Tolisso; Nuamah, Merah, Nakamura

Lyon's recent dominance in this fixture makes the visitors difficult to dismiss, particularly with Vicens hoping to make an immediate impression in his first match at the helm.

However, Lille's superior defensive record, unbeaten home form and greater consistency in the league should give Ancelotti's side the edge, and we expect the hosts to secure a narrow victory.

#2179. Mazzara: ‘A core of 16-18 high level players’ – Cardinale hopes to take Milan to new levels

Gerry Cardinale has invested heavily in AC Milan recently and there are no plans to slow down anytime soon.

Since the restructuring of the vendor loan, Cardinale has completely changed his ownership style. More actively involved, the American has seemingly fallen in love with the club and has become desperate to see it succeed.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Glimpses were seen before the mercato, with him regularly visiting the training ground. However, his work since then – spending €150 million on transfers and attending every Serie A game so far – shows the level of dedication he has to the cause.

In January, the American is expected to spend heavily, too. A €70 million bid for Endrick is being prepared, whilst he is also determined to sign Goncalo Inacio. It’s clear that he wants to raise the level of the starters and those who will contribute from the bench.

In an editorial for MilanNews today, Pietro Mazzara looked at the current squad and what Cardinale plans to do.

“AC Milan’s transfer market is poised for significant events because Gerry Cardinale has no intention of stopping. His comments in recent days, both public and private, are a clear statement of what the AC Milan owner intends to do to bring AC Milan back to the top.

“Whether he succeeds or not will only be determined by time and the type of decisions he makes, but he certainly has the desire, vision, and financial resources. One can expect anything from someone who beat out Netflix for the Warner Bros. acquisition.

“Among the many things he has learned is that the climate of mediocrity surrounding results has undermined the mentality of a club and an environment that, instead, must strive to always be at the top.

“But returning to those levels requires several factors: a clear decision-making structure (which will be finalised by Markus Krösche, who will always report to Cardinale, who will always have the final say and be involved in negotiations), strong players in the squad, a political presence in the halls of power, a connection with the fans, and credibility.

“What may seem like slogans in themselves are actually manifestos that one can legitimately believe or not. The only way to evaluate Cardinale’s work is to observe how he operates and then draw conclusions.

“He’s fired up, and between January and next summer there will be some serious transfer campaigns. The reason is simple: there’s a need to significantly raise the squad’s level, creating a core of 16-18 players of a certain caliber who can be joined by young players to develop and develop.

“This is why Milan will be looking for not only technically strong players, but also leaders who can complement those already in the Milan core group.

“It’s crucial to raise the team’s personality, including strong personalities who can provide a different kind of motivation during the day-to-day at Milanello. These players, inevitably, cost money, but Cardinale doesn’t want to set limits.

“This doesn’t mean Milan will sign a player worth one hundred million euros, but it does mean they can continue along the operational path laid out by Diego Moreira. All of this is in concert and in line with Ruben Amorim, who is fiercely defended by the AC Milan owner and with whom he intends to begin a long-term relationship.

“And the vision is to acquire the Van Dijks in the pre-prime phase rather than signing them at 35 (assuming, for the sake of argument, that I’d sign someone like that now).

“In my opinion, a Sandro Tonali- style signing is needed. And it’s not out of the question that Milan could try to bring him back in the coming years, even though he currently plays for a club as complex to negotiate with as Tottenham.

“Meanwhile, discussions are ongoing to finalise the renewal of Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse.”

#2178. Tom Brady eyes stake in Premier League giants after Birmingham City departure

Birmingham City confirmed last week that Tom Brady’s involvement with the club had come to an end. The former NFL star joined as part of Knighthead’s investment group following its takeover in 2023 and subsequently held a position on the Blues’ advisory board.

Brady has since spoken out on the ‘special club’ that Birmingham City is since his departure. However, he is already in talks to join another English club, with talks underway with Chelsea over a minority stake in the club, according to The Guardian.

The talks are said to be positive and he already has a strong relationship with Behdad Eghbali, whose fund Clearlake Capital owns 86.5% of Chelsea after Todd Boehly and Mark Walter sold their shares in September.

They have also said that has decision to sell his stake in BCFC, was too pursue the deal with Chelsea. Brady has previous with Chelsea, where he was a guest for the club as they won the Club World Cup back in the summer of 2025 and he was seen celebrating with the players.

While Brady was never a prominent member of the ownership around the club, he was the most well-known by some margin. That brought a lot of commercial benefits and a lot of eyes on the club, alongside their Amazon Prime series.

His departure did feel abrupt but now the reason is out, things start to make more sense. At the end of the day though, Brady brought eyes to the club and that has helped them keep the positivity flowing following their relegation in 2024.

Now, with BCFC flying at the top end of the Championship, Brady’s was no longer required. Selling his stake to buy one in Chelsea makes sense, considering his lack of real involvement with Birmingham City.

For Birmingham City, outside noise may not be what they need right now. Brady moving on will take a lot of that away, especially from outside of the UK.

However, their sole focus should be on what is happening on the pitch, not anything off the field. Chris Davies’ side return from the international break with a massive top of the table clash away at Stoke City.

BCFC know that a defeat to Stoke will mean they leapfrog them in the table. With the Blues currently top of the table, that is not what they would want, especially given Middlesbrough and Wolves could also go above them with wins this weekend.

#2176. Doncaster Rovers can’t be blinded by Grant McCann evidence as decision looms

Grant McCann’s return to Doncaster Rovers has been an undoubted success, but the cracks are beginning to show.

Rovers have slumped into the relegation zone of League One, been embarrassed by non-league opposition in the FA Cup, and lacked the signs of a team who could improve.

McCann’s men are flailing. They have won just one of their most recent five league fixtures. That was an impressive victory against a sub-par Sheffield Wednesday side, who sacked Henrik Pedersen in the aftermath.

They have shipped six goals away to Milton Keynes Dons, three at Luton Town, and a further three at Kidderminster Harriers. The latter saw them exit from the FA Cup at the first time of asking, further worsening their away form.

In the league, Rovers have won just once away from home this season, losing five and drawing the other of their seven trips. Their xG does place them 16th in the table, but their xG conceded puts them in the relegation zone with poor defensive statistics in particular, according to FotMob.

League One relegation zone as of November 19

No one has scored more than three goals for them in league action so far this term, with a form in parallel to the run that was play-off worthy form after the closure of the January transfer window last term.

That is the key for McCann. The form of his Doncaster team in the second half of campaigns.

Rovers collected 30 points in the last 18 games of the 2025/26 season, with only five teams managing more. That included both automatically promoted sides, and two of the teams who finished inside the play-offs alongside one who landed just outside.

It was the same the prior season, with their form after the closure of the January transfer window better than everyone else in League Two on route to their title win.

That theme can be stretched even further back, with the 2024/25 season seeing Doncaster manage the best record of any team in the fourth tier between the beginning of February and end of the campaign. That included a perfect home record of eight wins from eight, and only a single loss away from the then Eco-Power Stadium.

That season may have ended in bitter disappointment, with a penalty shootout defeat to Crawley Town in the semi-finals of the play-offs, but it was the first of three consecutive campaigns where post-January results had fixed a problem caused by early-season woes.

This time around it feels different. Chunks of the Doncaster fanbase have turned on McCann, not for the first time, with pointed chants directed at the Rovers manager following their chastening loss at Kidderminister. The dressing room and then the boardroom could follow suit if results, and performances, do not turn in the right direction.

We rank all 24 League One stadiums by their ground's distance from the city or town, starting with the longest distance.

The fixture list has not been kind either, with high-flying trio Bradford City, Reading, and league-leaders Huddersfield Town the next three opponents for the struggling Doncaster. McCann needs to get his team creating more chances, finishing them at a more consistent rate, and defending in a more cohesive and structured manner at the opposite end of the pitch.

To expect a trend to continue for a fourth season in a row might be asking for one too many miracles. If underwhelming performances continue to stack up and points continue to be lost, then Rovers could end up in a hole that even the fortunes of McCann’s recent second-half of the season displays can not dig them out of.
